results.title: Laboratory Specimen Acceptance Criteria - Lab Tests
results.content: Laboratory Specimen Acceptance Criteria 1. Specimen Labeling Specimens submitted for laboratory testing/analysis must be appropriately collected and properly and legibly labeled. 1. The patient’s first and last name must be on the specimen. 2. The medical record number (or downtime account number) must be on the specimen. 3. The date (MM/DD/YY) and time of collection as well as the collector’s name or initials must be on the specimen. 6. The patient information on the specimen must match the information on the label or requisition. Patient name and medical record (or downtime account) number. These must match the specimen. f. Patient information, such as patient age and/or date of birth, gender, etc., in order to provide appropriate reference ranges. Unacceptable Specimens Specimens that do not meet the acceptance criteria will be canceled and patient charges will be credited, if applicable. Specimens that are rejected due to patient identification problems are reported in the Patient Safety Network (PSN).

results.content:
Title: 790500: Clobazam and Desmethylclobazam, serum or plasma | MedTox
## Secondary navigation. + Medical Drug Monitoring & Pain Management. + Clinical Toxicology & Therapeutic Drug Monitoring. + Forensic Toxicology & Employment Drug Testing. + Medical Drug Monitoring & Toxicology Q&A. 3. / 790500: Clobazam and Desmethylclobazam, serum or plasma. # Clobazam and Desmethylclobazam, serum or plasma. ### Synonyms. ### Expected Turnaround Time. Turnaround time is defined as the usual number of days from the date of pickup of a specimen for testing to when the result is released to the ordering provider. In some cases, additional time should be allowed for additional confirmatory or additional reflex tests. ### Related Information. ## Specimen Requirements. ### Specimen. ### Volume. ### Minimum Volume. ### Container. Red-top (no additive) tube or green-top (heparin) tube. Gel-barrier tubes are not recommended. ### Collection. Transfer separated serum or plasma to a plastic transport tube. Trough levels are most reproducible. ### Storage Instructions. Submission/transport (<3 days): Room temperature. For storage beyond three days, specimen should be refrigerated or frozen. ## Test Details. Liquid chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry (LC/MS-MS). ### Reference Interval. Clobazam: 30 - 300 ng/mL; Desmethylclobazam: 300 - 3000 ng/mL.

In some cases, additional time should be allowed for additional confirmatory or additional reflex tests. ### Related Information. ## Specimen Requirements. ### Specimen. ### Volume. ### Minimum Volume. ### Container.
